subject: Shopscape launch — rate window orchestration and product asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc:
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Shopscape launch — rate window orchestration and product asks

Team —

Quick heads-up: Shopscape confirmed their public launch window for May 13–15 and asked us to support an ingress spike during the first 72 hours. They provided an initial traffic forecast (attached). High-level ask: a temporary rate uplift and a short-lived higher concurrency window for the first three days to avoid throttling noise while they warm up caches.

Numbers from their forecast (QPS mapped to Redwood tokens):
- Baseline steady-state: ~120 rps (500k tokens/day)
- Launch peak (hours 0–8 each day): up to 1,600 rps (6M tokens/day slice)
- Expected burst pattern: 10–20 min microspikes up to 2,400 rps

What I need by EOD tomorrow (Apr 12):
1) Product (Irene): is there a safe, supported config to enable a temporary short-lived "launch window" in the routing layer that increases per-customer concurrency and bypasses the soft rate floor for 72h? If not, what minimal product changes or runbook actions do we need?
2) Infra (David): what capacity headroom is realistic in us-west-2 for this profile? Can we commit to an automated bump and rollback?
3) Sales/SE (Karthik): confirm the commitment level (deal_id attached) — what SLA/credits are we offering if we make an exception?
4) CS (Neha): can you validate the load pattern with Shopscape and confirm they will stagger rollouts by region?

Attachments: shopscape_traffic_forecast_q2.csv, mutual_action_plan_v2.docx

Goal: agree on a single cross-functional plan (capacity bump amount, routing changes, rollback triggers, and customer preflight checklist) so I can reply with a single authoritative plan to Shopscape and include our mitigation guarantees.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shopscape launch — rate window orchestration and product asks

Marissa —

I validated the commercial side with Shopscape (Alex Wong). Deal SS-2024-4781 includes a short-term launch support clause we can activate. I'm proposing the following for tradeoffs:
- Offer a 72-hour "launch window" with a paid bump to a dedicated burst entitlement (three-day add-on).
- If we take the bump, give Shopscape a one-time 10% service credit if we breach RTT or incur more than two 5-minute escalations.

I'll own customer communication and signatures. Can we confirm the technical feasibility first? If the routing layer requires a product change, we need a short runbook instead of a product toggle.

Karthik
Senior Account Executive

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 14:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shopscape launch — rate window orchestration and product asks

Thanks for the context. Short answer: we don't have a single "launch window" toggle today, but we can accomplish the same outcome with a combination of routing policy flags + temporary higher concurrency on a customer tag. Options:

Option A (fastest, lowest dev churn):
- Product: add a customer-level routing policy for Shopscape to: increase max_concurrency to 4x for 72h and allow larger batch sizes for small-latency-sensitive calls.
- Requires a config change in the control plane only (no code deploy), with the policy attached to their customer id.
- Rollback: revert config.
- Caveat: will increase tail latency risk if overall cluster utilization is high. Need infra confirmation of headroom.

Option B (safer, needs infra help):
- Move Shopscape traffic onto a reserved capacity pool (hot-pool) for 72h. Requires creation of temporary capacity and routing to pool. This gives better isolation but needs infra to stand up GPUs and steering.

Product asks for infra: do we have an automated way to create temporary reserved pool and programmatically route? If not, David — can ops spin a hot-pool with minimal manual steps?

Also: we should require Shopscape to enable prefix caching and use our guidance to pre-warm KV cache for their most common prompt templates. I can draft the exact config and preflight checklist for them if we commit to approach A or B.

Irene
Director, Product Management

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2024 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shopscape launch — rate window orchestration and product asks

Team —

Short version: we can support Option A immediately via control-plane config, but only if we accept conservative limits and a preflight warmup. Option B (reserved hot-pool) is safer but will take ~18–24 hours to provision if we have spare quota in us-west-2.

Details:
- Current baseline cluster utilization (us-west-2 prod fleet): ~62%. We can absorb a steady-state uplift to ~75% with a short burst cushion for 72h if we schedule evening remediation windows and keep other noisy customers throttled.
- Suggested committed bump: +3x baseline concurrency for Shopscape during 0–72h, capped by a token ceiling of 7.5M tokens/day. That gives headroom for the predicted 6M/day peak and safety margin.
- Microspike protection: enable per-request rejection with 429s when seen + short backoff guidance to client.
- Rollback triggers (automated): cluster CPU/GPU utilization > 85% sustained for 5m; error rate > 3% for 10m; or tail latency p95 > 3x baseline for 10m. On trigger, we will automatically revert the concurrency bump and shift traffic to standard routing and notify SRE + Sales.

Operational asks:
1) CS to confirm Shopscape will run the warmup script (Neha).
2) Sales to approve the customer credit SLA (Karthik).
3) Product to produce the exact control-plane policy and the flag names (Irene).

I'll prep a short runbook for on-call to apply the config and rollback. Can have it ready by EOD today.

-David
Head of Infrastructure

From: Alex Wong <alex.wong@shopscape.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@shopscape.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Apr 2024 16:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Shopscape launch — rate window orchestration and product asks

Hi Marissa / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming Shopscape will:
- Run the warmup script across our staging fleet on May 6–7 (we'll share results).
- Accept a staged rollout regionally (US west -> US central -> US east) to smooth peak.
- Agree to the proposed token ceiling of 7.5M/day for the 72h window.

Small ask from our side: can Redwood provide a short preflight acceptance test (3 endpoints, 1k calls each) and a fill-in-the-blank mutual action checkbox list we can sign? Procurement needs that to finalize the small addendum.

Alex Wong
Head of Platform
Shopscape
